name: Ray Traversal and Coherency
text:
# Ray Traversal and Coherency

Also called: First Depth Ray Traversal

## Overview
This family accelerates [isosurface extraction](#30-isosurface-extraction.md) by optimizing the order and grouping of ray-volume interactions to minimize redundant traversal and intersection tests. It differs from naive uniform marching by using hierarchical [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) structures (octrees, tiled grids) and spatial coherence (ray packets) to skip empty space and process multiple rays simultaneously.

## Shared principles
The family shares the core mechanism of [Isosurface and first-hit ray casting](20-isosurface-and-first-hit-ray-casting.md): constructing a ray per pixel and finding the first point where $f(\mathbf{p}) \ge \tau$ or a sign change occurs [S3, unofficial][S1, unofficial]. Upon detection, the intersection is refined (e.g., linear interpolation) and shaded using $\nabla f$ [S3, unofficial][S1, unofficial]. The key distinction is the **traversal strategy**: instead of marching voxel-by-voxel, rays are accelerated by:
1.  **Hierarchical Culling:** Using min-max bounds in octrees or tiled grids to skip entire sub-volumes where $\tau \notin [min, max]$ [S1, unofficial][S2].
2.  **Coherence Exploitation:** Grouping rays into packets (e.g., 2x2) to traverse the acceleration structure together, leveraging spatial locality [S1, unofficial].
3.  **List-Based Restriction:** Pre-computing a short, front-to-back list of candidate blocks/pixels for each ray, restricting the search space [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Cell-Based First-Hit Ray Casting](1039-cell-based-first-hit-ray-casting.md)
A technique using a min-max octree of macro-cells ($n^3$ cells, $n \in [3,10]$). It projects trimmed macro-cells to the screen, rasterizes them, and casts local rays only at uncolored pixels. It reduces ray path lengths via [early termination](#4675-early-termination.md) but suffers at low thresholds where "peep holes" delay termination.

### [Hybrid Strategy for Interactive High Resolution Isosurface Ray Tracing](3697-hybrid-strategy-for-interactive-high-resolution-isosurface-r.md)
Combines object-order projection with image-order [ray casting](#6080-ray-casting.md) on multi-core CPUs. Phase I identifies visible, isosurface-intersecting 3D tiles; Phase II dynamically allocates ray casting tasks to cores based on these candidate lists. It solves load-balancing issues of static partitioning but requires careful memory hierarchy management.

### [Interactive High Resolution Isosurface Ray Tracing](4093-interactive-high-resolution-isosurface-ray-tracing.md)
Uses a [Branch-On-Need Octree (BONO)](#6935-branch-on-need-octree-bono.md) to build front-to-back block lists per pixel, capped at size $k$ (typically $\le 20$). Phase I generates lists; Phase II casts rays through them. If the list fills, a resume point is stored for later traversal. It avoids [SIMD](#2564-voxel-trilinear-interpolation-simd.md) dependency by using algorithmic list merging, maintaining coherence on complex data.

### [Coherent Multiresolution Isosurface Ray Tracing](4095-coherent-multiresolution-isosurface-ray-tracing.md)
Groups rays into 2x2 packets to traverse a multiresolution octree. It uses an LOD cut depth to switch between fine voxels and coarser cells, maintaining coherence even in large volumes. SSE optimizations accelerate intersection tests within leaf nodes.

### First Depth Ray Traversal
A [ray traversal scheme](#6890-ray-traversal-schemes.md) that extracts iso-surfaces, introduced by Tuy & Tuy in 1984 [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The "First Depth" or "First Intensity" traversal strategy was introduced by Tuy and Tuy in 1984 to extract isosurfaces [S1, unofficial]. This approach contrasts with accumulation-based methods (like Levoy’s 1988 [compositing](#2436-compositing.md)) by stopping at the first surface hit [S1, unofficial]. Modern implementations leverage octrees and ray coherence to make this interactive on large datasets [S1, unofficial].
